en: She whose jar-like breasts are beautiful, who holds a jar filled with nectar, who is supported by grace, who is supported by great merit,
whose moon-disk face is ever-present, and whose bimba-fruit lips are always present.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||1||
With a sidelong glance moist with compassion, holding the gesture of wisdom in her hand,
awakened by the arts, auspicious with her ornaments,
the woman who is foremost, sleepless, and more exalted than the city of Tuṅgabhadra.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||2||
Her forehead is marked with a tilaka, her limbs shine with radiant luster,
she is the sole protector of her devotees, and the beauty of her fame rests upon her cheeks; in her hand, she holds a rosary that gleams like ancient gold.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||3||
Her braid-parting is beautiful, her eyes have surpassed the female deer, her voice delights like that of a parrot, and she bows to the wielder of the thunderbolt;
with a face slow with nectar, she is a braid to be meditated upon with joy.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||4||
She who is perfectly tranquil, possessed of a beautiful body, whose hair ends at the corners of her eyes, whose limbs are like shimmering, excellent creepers, infinite and inconceivable—
her, who existed before creation and is remembered by ascetics.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||5||
I always worship her who is in the form of the Goddess, mounted upon a deer, a horse, a lion, a king of birds, a swan, an elephant in rut, and a great bull,
on the great ninth lunar day.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||6||
I worship her whose body enchants the world like a blazing fire of splendor,
who is like a bee hovering over the lotus of my mind,
and whose limbs shine with the song and dance of her own hymn of praise.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||7||
She was being worshipped by the King of the Lotus-Eyed One (Viṣṇu),
her face marked by the radiance of a shimmering, gentle smile,
and her ears adorned with swinging, flickering, and beautiful earrings.
I worship Śāradāmbā, my mother, incessantly. ||8||

Thus ends "The Octave of the Śāradā-Courtesan" composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, the wandering ascetic teacher (parivrājaka-ācārya) of the illustrious supreme state, and the disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda.
